description: Comprehensive knowledge base for Accounting-related support questions

articles.title: How to Submit an Invoice
articles.question: How do I submit an invoice for payment?
articles.content:
## Invoice Submission Process

**Required Information:**
- Vendor name and details
- Invoice number and date
- PO number (if applicable)
- Amount and currency
- Payment terms

**Steps:**
1. Log into the **Finance Portal**
2. Navigate to **Invoices > Submit New**
3. Upload the invoice PDF or image
4. Fill in the required fields
5. Select the appropriate cost center
6. Submit for approval

**Processing Time:** 5-7 business days after approval

**Questions?** Contact accounts.payable@company.com

articles.title: Expense Report Submission
articles.question: How do I submit an expense report?
articles.content:
## Expense Report Process

**What's Reimbursable:**
- Travel expenses (flights, hotels, meals)
- Client entertainment
- Office supplies
- Training materials

**Steps:**
1. Open the **Expense Management System**
2. Create a new expense report
3. Add each expense with:
   - Date and description
   - Amount and category
   - Receipt photo/PDF
4. Link to project code if applicable
5. Submit for manager approval

**Important:**
- Submit within 30 days of expense
- Keep original receipts
- Per diem rates apply for meals

**Reimbursement Timeline:** 7-10 business days after approval

articles.title: Budget Approval Process
articles.question: How does the budget approval process work?
articles.content:
## Budget Approval Workflow

**Approval Thresholds:**
| Amount | Approver |
|--------|----------|
| < $1,000 | Manager |
| $1,000 - $10,000 | Director |
| $10,000 - $50,000 | VP |
| > $50,000 | CFO |

**Process:**
1. Create a budget request in the Finance Portal
2. Attach justification and quotes
3. Submit to your direct manager
4. Approval routes automatically based on amount
5. You'll receive email notification when approved

**Tips:**
- Include ROI analysis for large requests
- Get quotes from multiple vendors
- Plan ahead - approvals take 3-5 business days

articles.title: Purchase Order Process
articles.question: How do I create a purchase order?
articles.content:
## Creating a Purchase Order

**When You Need a PO:**
- Purchases over $500
- Recurring vendor services
- Capital equipment

**Steps:**
1. Go to **Procurement Portal**
2. Select **Create Purchase Requisition**
3. Enter vendor and item details
4. Add budget code and cost center
5. Attach quotes (required for purchases > $2,500)
6. Submit for approval

**After Approval:**
- PO number is generated automatically
- Share PO number with the vendor
- Goods receipt required upon delivery

**Turnaround:** 2-3 business days for approval

articles.title: Payroll Questions
articles.question: Where can I view my pay stub?
articles.content:
## Payroll Information

**View Pay Stubs:**
1. Log into the **HR Portal**
2. Navigate to **My Pay > Pay Statements**
3. Select the pay period to view

**Direct Deposit Changes:**
- Go to **My Profile > Payment Methods**
- Updates take effect next pay cycle
- Allow 1-2 pay periods for verification

**Payroll Schedule:**
- Pay periods: Bi-weekly (every other Friday)
- Cut-off: Tuesday before payday

**Questions about deductions?**
Contact HR at hr@company.com or ext. 2100

articles.title: Tax Documents
articles.question: Where do I get my tax documents?
articles.content:
## Tax Document Access

**W-2 Forms:**
- Available by January 31st each year
- Access via **HR Portal > Tax Documents**
- Mailed copies sent to address on file

**Updating Tax Withholding:**
1. Log into HR Portal
2. Go to **My Profile > Tax Withholding**
3. Complete a new W-4 form
4. Changes apply to next paycheck

**1099 Contractors:**
- Available by January 31st
- Access via contractor portal

**Need Prior Year Documents?**
Contact HR - we retain records for 7 years.

articles.title: Corporate Credit Card
articles.question: How do I get and use a corporate credit card?
articles.content:
## Corporate Credit Card Guide

**Requesting a Card:**
1. Submit request through Finance Portal
2. Requires manager and Finance approval
3. Card arrives in 5-7 business days

**Card Limits:**
- Standard: $5,000/month
- Higher limits require VP approval

**Required Documentation:**
- Receipts for ALL transactions
- Business purpose for each charge
- Monthly reconciliation due by 5th of each month

**Prohibited Uses:**
- Personal expenses
- Cash advances
- Entertainment over $200 without pre-approval

**Lost or Stolen Card:**
Call the bank immediately, then notify Finance.

articles.title: Vendor Setup and Management
articles.question: How do I set up a new vendor?
articles.content:
## New Vendor Setup

**Required Documents:**
- W-9 form (for US vendors)
- Bank details for ACH payment
- Insurance certificate (if applicable)
- Signed contract/agreement

**Process:**
1. Submit **Vendor Request Form** in Finance Portal
2. Vendor receives onboarding email
3. Vendor completes registration
4. Finance reviews and approves
5. Vendor available for POs within 2-3 days

**International Vendors:**
- Additional documentation required
- May require wire transfer setup
- Allow extra processing time

**Preferred Vendors:**
Check the approved vendor list before engaging new suppliers.

articles.title: Cost Center and GL Codes
articles.question: What cost center or GL code should I use?
articles.content:
## Cost Center & GL Code Guide

**Finding Your Cost Center:**
- Listed on your department's budget report
- Ask your manager if unsure
- Format: XXX-XXXX (Dept-Project)

**Common GL Codes:**
| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 6010 | Office Supplies |
| 6020 | Software/Subscriptions |
| 6030 | Travel - Airfare |
| 6040 | Travel - Lodging |
| 6050 | Travel - Meals |
| 6100 | Professional Services |
| 6200 | Training & Development |
| 6300 | Marketing & Advertising |

**Full List:**
Available in Finance Portal > Resources > Chart of Accounts

**Wrong Code Used?**
Submit a journal entry request to correct it.

articles.title: Journal Entry Request
articles.question: How do I request a journal entry or correction?
articles.content:
## Journal Entry Requests

**When Needed:**
- Correct coding errors
- Transfer costs between departments
- Record accruals or adjustments
- Reclassify expenses

**How to Request:**
1. Go to Finance Portal > Journal Entries
2. Complete the request form
3. Include:
   - From/To accounts
   - Amount
   - Description/justification
   - Supporting documentation
4. Submit for approval

**Approval Required:**
- All entries require Finance approval
- Entries over $10,000 require Controller approval

**Timing:**
- Month-end cut-off is 3rd business day
- Year-end entries have earlier deadlines

articles.title: Invoice Payment Status
articles.question: How do I check if an invoice has been paid?
articles.content:
## Checking Payment Status

**In Finance Portal:**
1. Go to **Accounts Payable > Invoice Search**
2. Enter invoice number or vendor name
3. View status: Pending, Approved, Paid
4. See payment date and check/transfer number

**Payment Schedule:**
- Standard terms: Net 30
- Payment runs: Every Tuesday and Friday
- ACH transfers: 2-3 days to clear
- Checks: 5-7 days to arrive

**Vendor Inquiries:**
If a vendor asks about payment:
1. Verify the invoice was submitted
2. Check if PO/approval is complete
3. Share expected payment date

**Rush Payments:**
Require VP approval and additional processing fee.

articles.title: Month-End Close Process
articles.question: What are the month-end close deadlines?
articles.content:
## Month-End Close Schedule

**Key Deadlines:**
| Day | Activity |
|-----|----------|
| Last day of month | Submit all invoices |
| 1st business day | Expense reports due |
| 2nd business day | Accrual submissions |
| 3rd business day | Journal entries due |
| 5th business day | Preliminary close |
| 10th business day | Final close |

**What You Need to Do:**
1. Submit pending expense reports
2. Approve invoices in your queue
3. Submit accruals for goods/services received but not invoiced
4. Review department budget vs actuals

**Year-End:**
- Deadlines are 1 week earlier
- Additional reconciliations required
- Audit preparation begins in January

articles.title: Travel Booking and Policy
articles.question: How do I book business travel?
articles.content:
## Business Travel Guide

**Booking Process:**
1. Get manager approval for the trip
2. Use the **Travel Portal** (preferred)
3. Or book directly and submit for reimbursement

**Policy Highlights:**
- Book flights 14+ days in advance when possible
- Economy class for domestic, premium for 6+ hours
- Hotels: Company-negotiated rates preferred
- Rental cars: Compact class unless justified

**Expense Limits:**
| Category | Limit |
|----------|-------|
| Meals (domestic) | $75/day |
| Meals (international) | $100/day |
| Hotel | $250/night (varies by city) |

**Required Receipts:**
- All expenses over $25
- Itemized receipts for meals
- Boarding passes for flights

articles.title: Mileage Reimbursement
articles.question: How do I get reimbursed for mileage?
articles.content:
## Mileage Reimbursement

**Current Rate:**
- IRS standard rate (check current year)
- Updated annually in January

**Eligible Travel:**
- Between work locations
- Client visits
- Business errands

**NOT Reimbursable:**
- Commuting to/from your regular office
- Personal stops during business travel

**How to Submit:**
1. Go to Expense Portal
2. Create new expense > Mileage
3. Enter start/end addresses
4. System calculates distance and amount
5. Add to expense report

**Documentation:**
- Date and purpose of trip
- Starting and ending location
- Business reason

**Tips:** Use Google Maps to verify distances if questioned.

articles.title: Budget Transfer Request
articles.question: How do I transfer budget between accounts?
articles.content:
## Budget Transfer Process

**When Allowed:**
- Between line items in same cost center
- Between cost centers with approvals
- Cannot increase total annual budget

**To Request:**
1. Go to **Finance Portal > Budget > Transfers**
2. Select source and destination accounts
3. Enter amount and justification
4. Attach supporting documentation
5. Submit for approval

**Approval Requirements:**
- Within cost center: Manager approval
- Between cost centers: Both managers + Finance
- Over $50,000: CFO approval

**Timing:**
- Standard: 3-5 business days
- Fiscal year-end: Submit 2 weeks before close

**Note:** Some budget categories cannot be transferred (headcount, capital).

articles.title: Accounts Receivable - Customer Payment
articles.question: How do I record a customer payment or check AR status?
articles.content:
## Accounts Receivable Guide

**Check Customer Balance:**
1. Go to Finance Portal > AR Dashboard
2. Search by customer name or invoice
3. View outstanding invoices and aging

**Recording Payments:**
- Payments received via lockbox are auto-posted
- Other payments: Submit to ar@company.com
- Include customer name, amount, invoice number

**Collection Process:**
| Days | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1-30 | Standard terms |
| 31-60 | Reminder sent |
| 61-90 | Collection call |
| 90+ | Escalation to management |

**Customer Disputes:**
Log in Finance Portal with details for investigation

**Credit Memos:**
Require manager approval before issuance.

articles.title: Fixed Asset and Capital Purchases
articles.question: How do I purchase or track fixed assets?
articles.content:
## Fixed Asset Process

**What's a Fixed Asset?**
- Equipment/furniture over $5,000
- Useful life over 1 year
- Computers, vehicles, machinery

**Purchasing:**
1. Create capital expenditure request
2. Requires budget approval
3. Multi-year impact analysis needed
4. VP/CFO approval for large purchases

**After Purchase:**
- Finance assigns asset tag
- Record in fixed asset system
- Annual physical inventory required

**Depreciation:**
- Calculated monthly by Finance
- Follows company policy and tax rules

**Disposal:**
- Submit Asset Disposal Form
- IT wipes data from electronics
- Finance records gain/loss

articles.title: Petty Cash Reimbursement
articles.question: How do I get petty cash reimbursement?
articles.content:
## Petty Cash Process

**Eligibility:**
- Small purchases under $50
- When corporate card not accepted
- Emergency supplies

**To Request Reimbursement:**
1. Complete Petty Cash Voucher
2. Attach original receipt
3. Get manager signature
4. Submit to Finance office

**Reimbursement Methods:**
- Cash from petty cash custodian
- Add to expense report for payroll

**Petty Cash Custodians:**
- Each department has assigned custodian
- Check Finance Portal for your area

**Not Allowed:**
- Personal items
- Gifts over $25
- Items that should use PO process

**Replenishment:**
Custodians submit for replenishment at $100 balance.

articles.title: Intercompany Transactions
articles.question: How do I handle intercompany transactions?
articles.content:
## Intercompany Transactions

**What Are They?**
- Transactions between company entities
- Must follow transfer pricing policies
- Require proper documentation

**Types:**
- Shared services allocation
- Inventory transfers
- Management fees
- Loan repayments

**Process:**
1. Initiate through Intercompany module
2. Both entities must approve
3. Matching entries created automatically
4. Finance reconciles monthly

**Documentation Required:**
- Service agreement or invoice
- Pricing methodology
- Supporting calculations

**Timing:**
- Submit by 5th of month for prior month
- Quarter-end has earlier deadlines

**Questions?** Contact corporate.accounting@company.com

articles.title: Bonus and Commission Payments
articles.question: How are bonuses and commissions processed?
articles.content:
## Bonus & Commission Payments

**Annual Bonuses:**
- Calculated based on performance review
- Approved by HR and Finance
- Typically paid in Q1 (Feb/March)
- Subject to applicable taxes

**Sales Commissions:**
- Calculated monthly based on closed deals
- Submitted by Sales Operations
- Paid following month payroll
- Commission statements available in HR Portal

**Spot Bonuses:**
- Manager can award for exceptional performance
- Requires HR and Finance approval
- Processed in next payroll cycle

**Taxes:**
- Bonuses taxed at supplemental rate
- May differ from regular paycheck

**Questions:**
Commission disputes: sales.ops@company.com
Bonus questions: hr@company.com

articles.title: Chart of Accounts Changes
articles.question: How do I request a new GL account or code?
articles.content:
## Requesting New GL Accounts

**When Needed:**
- New product line or service
- New department or project
- Regulatory requirement
- Improved reporting granularity

**Process:**
1. Submit Chart of Accounts Change Request
2. Include:
   - Account name and description
   - Business justification
   - Reporting requirements
   - Affected departments
3. Controller reviews and approves
4. Account created within 2-3 days

**Naming Convention:**
- Follow existing numbering scheme
- Finance assigns final number
- Description must be clear and consistent

**Note:** Quarterly review may consolidate unused accounts.

**For cost centers:** Similar process through FP&A team.

articles.title: Audit Support and Documentation
articles.question: What documentation do I need for an audit?
articles.content:
## Audit Documentation Guide

**Common Requests:**
- Invoice and payment backup
- Contract copies
- Approval evidence (emails, signatures)
- Reconciliations
- Vendor agreements

**How to Prepare:**
1. Keep organized records throughout the year
2. Respond to auditor requests within 48 hours
3. Provide complete documentation
4. Don't alter or backdate documents

**SOX Controls:**
- Follow all documented procedures
- Maintain segregation of duties
- Evidence all approvals
- Report exceptions promptly

**Audit Types:**
- External: Annual financial audit
- Internal: Quarterly process audits
- SOX: Continuous control testing

**During Audit:**
- Be available for walkthrough meetings
- Answer questions honestly
- Escalate concerns to management

articles.title: Foreign Currency Transactions
articles.question: How do I handle foreign currency invoices?
articles.content:
## Foreign Currency Guide

**Invoice Submission:**
1. Submit invoice in original currency
2. System converts at daily rate
3. Payment made in vendor's currency

**Exchange Rates:**
- Updated daily from bank feed
- Month-end rate used for accruals
- Gain/loss recorded automatically

**Expense Reports:**
- Enter in currency spent
- Attach credit card statement showing conversion
- Personal card charges: use bank rate

**Wire Transfers:**
- May have bank fees ($25-50)
- Allow 3-5 days for international
- Large transfers need Treasury approval

**Hedging:**
- Finance hedges significant exposures
- Do not commit to fixed exchange rates without Treasury approval

**Questions:** treasury@company.com

articles.title: Prepaid Expenses and Amortization
articles.question: How do I handle prepaid expenses?
articles.content:
## Prepaid Expenses Guide

**What's a Prepaid?**
- Payment made for future periods
- Examples: Annual insurance, subscriptions, rent

**Threshold:**
- Amounts > $5,000 and > 1 month period
- Smaller amounts can expense immediately

**Process:**
1. Invoice coded to prepaid asset account
2. Finance creates amortization schedule
3. Monthly expense recognized automatically
4. Review schedule in Finance Portal

**Common Prepaids:**
| Type | Amortization Period |
|------|--------------------|
| Insurance | 12 months |
| Software licenses | Contract term |
| Rent deposits | Lease term |
| Conferences | 1 month before event |

**Your Responsibility:**
Notify Finance when prepaid invoices are processed.

articles.title: Bank Account Changes
articles.question: How do I update banking information?
articles.content:
## Bank Account Updates

**For Direct Deposit (Employee):**
1. Log into HR Portal
2. Go to **My Profile > Payment Methods**
3. Enter new bank details
4. Verify with micro-deposits
5. Changes take 1-2 pay cycles

**For Vendor Payments:**
- Vendor updates through vendor portal
- Changes require verification call
- Allow 2-3 days processing

**Company Bank Accounts:**
- Only Treasury can modify
- Submit request to treasury@company.com
- New accounts need CFO approval

**Security:**
- Never share bank details via email
- Verify any bank change requests by phone
- Report suspicious requests immediately

**Wire Instructions:**
- Provided only through secure portal
- Confirm large wires by phone callback

articles.title: Data Entry Errors
articles.question: How do I fix data entry errors in accounting?
articles.content:
## Fixing Data Entry Errors

**Common Error Types:**
- Transposed digits (e.g., 54 vs 45)
- Decimal point errors
- Missed entries
- Wrong account coding

**Prevention:**
1. Double-check all manual entries
2. Use automated data capture when possible
3. Implement verification checkpoints
4. Review reports for anomalies

**How to Correct:**
1. **Same Period:** Void and re-enter the transaction
2. **Closed Period:** Submit journal entry correction
3. **Material Errors:** Notify Finance immediately

**Documentation Required:**
- Original entry details
- Correct entry details
- Reason for error
- Approval from manager

**Impact:**
Data entry errors can affect financial statements, tax calculations, and business decisions. Report and correct promptly.

articles.title: Expense Classification Errors
articles.question: I coded an expense to the wrong category
articles.content:
## Expense Classification Guide

**Common Classification Issues:**
- Capital vs Operating expenses
- Direct vs Indirect costs
- Travel vs Entertainment
- Wrong department coding

**Why It Matters:**
- Affects financial statements accuracy
- Impacts tax calculations
- Skews budget reports
- May violate policies

**How to Correct:**
1. Submit reclassification request
2. Provide correct category/account
3. Include business justification
4. Finance processes within 2-3 days

**Classification Guidelines:**
| Expense Type | GL Category |
|--------------|-------------|
| Equipment >$5K | Capital |
| Equipment <$5K | Operating |
| Training | Professional Dev |
| Client meals | Entertainment |

**When Unsure:** Contact Finance before submitting, not after!

articles.title: Unauthorized Purchases
articles.question: What happens if I make an unauthorized purchase?
articles.content:
## Unauthorized Purchase Policy

**What's Unauthorized?**
- Purchases without required approval
- Exceeding spending limits
- Bypassing PO process
- Using personal funds without pre-approval

**Consequences:**
- Reimbursement may be denied
- Budget impact to your department
- Policy violation on record
- Repeated violations may affect performance review

**How to Resolve:**
1. Document the business justification
2. Obtain retroactive approval (if possible)
3. Submit with explanation to Finance
4. Manager must approve exception

**Prevention:**
- Know your spending authority limits
- When in doubt, get approval FIRST
- Use corporate card with proper controls
- Follow PO process for large purchases

**Emergency Purchases:**
Contact Finance for expedited approval process.

articles.title: Lost Receipts
articles.question: I lost my receipt - what do I do?
articles.content:
## Lost Receipt Procedure

**First, Try to Recover:**
1. Check email for digital receipts
2. Request duplicate from vendor
3. Check credit card statements
4. Look for bank transaction record

**If Truly Lost:**
1. Complete **Lost Receipt Affidavit**
2. Include:
   - Date of purchase
   - Vendor name
   - Amount
   - Business purpose
3. Get manager signature
4. Submit with expense report

**Limitations:**
- Affidavit limit: $75 per expense
- Maximum 3 per quarter
- Frequent lost receipts may require additional approval

**Prevention Tips:**
- Photograph receipts immediately
- Use expense app to capture receipts
- Request email receipts when possible
- Keep receipts in one designated place

**Tax Implications:** IRS requires documentation. Lost receipts may not be tax-deductible.

articles.title: Expense Fraud Prevention
articles.question: How does the company prevent expense fraud?
articles.content:
## Expense Fraud Prevention

**Types of Expense Fraud:**
- Inflated expense amounts
- Fabricated receipts
- Personal purchases claimed as business
- Duplicate submissions
- Mileage padding

**Our Controls:**
1. Receipt verification
2. Manager approval required
3. Random audits by Finance
4. Automated duplicate detection
5. Spending pattern analysis

**Consequences of Fraud:**
- Immediate termination
- Required repayment
- Possible legal action
- Reported to authorities if criminal

**Reporting Suspected Fraud:**
- Ethics hotline: ethics@company.com
- Anonymous reporting available
- No retaliation for good-faith reports

**Your Responsibility:**
- Submit honest expenses only
- Report suspicious activity
- Keep accurate records
- Follow all expense policies

articles.title: Duplicate Invoice Payments
articles.question: We accidentally paid an invoice twice
articles.content:
## Duplicate Payment Recovery

**How It Happens:**
- Same invoice submitted multiple times
- Invoice number entered incorrectly
- Multiple people processing same invoice
- Vendor resubmits unpaid invoice

**To Report:**
1. Contact AP immediately: ap@company.com
2. Provide invoice numbers and payment details
3. Include vendor contact information

**Recovery Process:**
1. Finance verifies duplicate payment
2. Contact vendor for refund or credit
3. Apply credit to future invoices
4. Or request check refund

**Prevention:**
- System checks for duplicate invoice numbers
- Three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice)
- Careful review before approval
- Standardized invoice numbering

**Timeline:** Recovery typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on vendor responsiveness.

articles.title: Late Bill Payments
articles.question: An invoice wasn't paid on time
articles.content:
## Late Payment Resolution

**Immediate Actions:**
1. Contact AP to check status
2. Identify cause of delay
3. Expedite payment if possible
4. Communicate with vendor

**Common Causes:**
- Stuck in approval queue
- Missing documentation
- PO discrepancy
- Invoice not properly submitted
- Budget issues

**Late Payment Consequences:**
- Late fees (typically 1-1.5% per month)
- Damaged vendor relationship
- Potential supply disruption
- Impact on credit terms

**Prevention:**
1. Submit invoices promptly
2. Approve quickly when in your queue
3. Ensure proper coding and PO
4. Set up recurring payments for regular vendors

**Rush Payment:** For urgent situations, contact Finance for expedited processing (additional fees may apply).

articles.title: Payment Approval Bottlenecks
articles.question: My invoice approval is stuck
articles.content:
## Resolving Approval Delays

**Check Status:**
1. Log into Finance Portal
2. Go to **Invoices > My Approvals**
3. See where invoice is in workflow
4. Identify current approver

**Common Bottlenecks:**
- Approver on vacation
- High volume periods
- Missing information
- Incorrect routing
- Amount exceeds authority

**To Expedite:**
1. Contact the approver directly
2. Provide business justification for urgency
3. Offer additional documentation if needed
4. If unavailable, request delegation

**Delegation Options:**
- Approvers can delegate during absences
- Finance can re-route with justification
- Manager can escalate to next level

**Prevention:**
- Submit invoices well before due date
- Ensure complete documentation upfront
- Use correct approval chain
- Set reminders for pending approvals

articles.title: Late Payments from Customers
articles.question: A customer hasn't paid their invoice
articles.content:
## Customer Payment Collection

**Payment Reminder Process:**
| Days Overdue | Action |
|--------------|--------|
| 1-7 days | Automatic reminder |
| 8-30 days | Follow-up call |
| 31-60 days | Formal collection letter |
| 61-90 days | Escalate to management |
| 90+ days | Consider collection agency |

**Before Escalating:**
1. Verify invoice was received
2. Check for disputes or issues
3. Confirm correct contact info
4. Review payment history

**Working with Customers:**
- Offer payment plans if needed
- Consider early payment discounts
- Maintain professional relationship
- Document all communications

**When to Involve Finance:**
- Payment disputes
- Need for credit holds
- Bad debt write-off consideration
- Legal collection action

**Contact:** ar@company.com for assistance

articles.title: Cash Flow Management
articles.question: How do I check or manage cash flow?
articles.content:
## Cash Flow Information

**For Department Managers:**
- Review monthly budget reports
- Monitor spending vs forecast
- Plan major purchases with Finance
- Submit accruals for upcoming expenses

**Cash Flow Visibility:**
1. Finance Portal > Treasury Dashboard
2. Weekly cash position report (distributed Mondays)
3. Monthly cash forecast (part of close package)

**Improving Cash Flow:**
- Collect receivables promptly
- Time large payments strategically
- Take advantage of early payment discounts
- Forecast major expenses

**Cash Flow Concerns:**
If you anticipate cash needs:
1. Notify Finance early
2. Provide timing and amounts
3. Include business justification
4. Plan for payment timing

**For Treasury Inquiries:** Contact treasury@company.com

articles.title: Recurring Payment Setup
articles.question: How do I set up recurring payments?
articles.content:
## Recurring Payment Setup

**Eligible Payments:**
- Monthly subscriptions
- Lease payments
- Retainer agreements
- Utility bills
- Ongoing services

**Setup Process:**
1. Complete Recurring Payment Form
2. Attach contract/agreement
3. Specify:
   - Vendor and amount
   - Frequency (monthly, quarterly, annual)
   - Start and end dates
   - GL coding
4. Submit for approval
5. Finance sets up automation

**Requirements:**
- Signed contract required
- Budget approval needed
- PO created for full contract value

**Changes to Recurring Payments:**
- Submit modification request
- Allow 5 business days notice
- Price changes require new approval

**Cancellation:**
Submit 30 days before next payment to stop.

articles.title: Invoice Disputes
articles.question: I need to dispute a vendor invoice
articles.content:
## Invoice Dispute Process

**When to Dispute:**
- Incorrect pricing
- Wrong quantities
- Services not received
- Quality issues
- Duplicate billing

**How to Dispute:**
1. Mark invoice as **Disputed** in Finance Portal
2. Select dispute reason
3. Add detailed explanation
4. Attach supporting documentation
5. Submit for AP review

**Documentation Needed:**
- Original PO or quote
- Contract terms
- Proof of issue (photos, emails)
- Correspondence with vendor

**Resolution Timeline:**
- Simple disputes: 5-10 business days
- Complex disputes: 2-4 weeks
- Legal involvement: Varies

**Partial Payments:**
AP may pay undisputed portion while resolving dispute.

**Your Role:** You may need to negotiate directly with vendor while AP holds payment.

articles.title: Year-End Closing Procedures
articles.question: What are the year-end closing procedures?
articles.content:
## Year-End Close Checklist

**Key Deadlines (Fiscal Year End):**
| Timing | Activity |
|--------|----------|
| -2 weeks | Submit all invoices |
| -1 week | Complete expense reports |
| Last day | Accruals and JEs due |
| +2 days | Preliminary close |
| +5 days | Final adjustments |
| +10 days | Year closed |

**Your Responsibilities:**
1. Submit pending expense reports
2. Approve all invoices in your queue
3. Review department spending for anomalies
4. Submit accruals for received but unbilled items
5. Complete fixed asset inventory

**Special Considerations:**
- No carryover of unused budget
- Capital purchases must be received
- Review prepaid schedules
- Confirm revenue recognition

**Late Submissions:**
Will be charged to new year - may require VP exception for prior year posting.

articles.title: Financial Reporting Access
articles.question: How do I access financial reports for my department?
articles.content:
## Financial Report Access

**Available Reports:**
- Budget vs Actual
- Spending by Category
- Vendor Spending Analysis
- Open PO Report
- Department P&L

**How to Access:**
1. Log into **Finance Portal**
2. Go to **Reports > Department Reports**
3. Select report type
4. Filter by date range and cost center
5. Export to Excel if needed

**Report Schedule:**
| Report | Frequency | Available |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| Flash Report | Weekly | Monday AM |
| Budget vs Actual | Monthly | Day 5 |
| Full Financials | Monthly | Day 10 |
| Forecast | Quarterly | Week 2 |

**Need Custom Reports?**
Submit request to Finance with:
- Data needed
- Purpose
- Frequency
- Recipients

**Training:** Monthly Finance Portal training available.

articles.title: Spending Controls and Limits
articles.question: What are my spending authority limits?
articles.content:
## Spending Authority Guide

**Standard Limits by Role:**
| Role | Single Purchase | Monthly |
|------|-----------------|----------|
| Staff | $500 | $2,000 |
| Manager | $2,500 | $10,000 |
| Director | $10,000 | $50,000 |
| VP | $50,000 | $200,000 |
| C-Level | Per policy | Unlimited |

**These Apply To:**
- Purchase requisitions
- Expense approval
- Corporate card limits
- Contract signing

**Exceeding Limits:**
- Requires next-level approval
- Document business justification
- May require additional quotes

**Delegation:**
- Can delegate during absences
- Must be pre-approved in system
- Cannot exceed your own limits

**Check Your Limits:**
Finance Portal > My Profile > Spending Authority

**Questions:** Contact your manager or Finance.
